questions.stem: Which of the following formulas should be used to calculate the economic rate of return on common stock?

choices.label: A
choices.text: (Dividends + change in price) divided by beginning price

choices.label: B
choices.text: (Net income - preferred dividend) divided by common shares outstanding

choices.label: C
choices.text: Market price per share divided by earnings per share

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dividends per share divided by market price per share

questions.explanation: The economic (total) rate of return captures everything the shareholder gains: cash dividends plus the change in market price, measured against what was invested at the start. Choice B is earnings per share, C is the price-earnings ratio, and D is the dividend yield, none of which include the capital gain.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的（総合）収益率は、株主が得るものすべて、すなわち現金配当と株価の変動を、期首の投資額に対して測る。選択肢Bは1株当たり利益、Cは株価収益率、Dは配当利回りであり、いずれも値上がり益を含んでいない。

questions.stem:
Salem Co. is considering a project that yields annual net cash inflows of $420,000 for years 1 through 5, and a net cash inflow of $100,000 in year 6. The project will require an initial investment of $1,800,000.
Salem's cost of capital is 10%. Present value information is presented below:
Present value of $1 for 5 years at 10% is .62.
Present value of $1 for 6 years at 10% is .56.
Present value of an annuity of $1 for 5 years at 10% is 3.79.
What was Salem's expected net present value for this project?
questions.explanation: Years 1-5 are a level annuity: $420,000 x 3.79 = $1,591,800. Year 6 is a single sum: $100,000 x 0.56 = $56,000. Total present value = $1,647,800, less the $1,800,000 investment = $(152,200). Note the 5-year single-sum factor 0.62 is a distractor and is not used.
questions.explanationJa: 1〜5年目は毎年一定の年金なので年金現価係数を使う: $420,000 × 3.79 = $1,591,800。6年目は一時金なので $100,000 × 0.56 = $56,000。現在価値合計 = $1,647,800、投資額 $1,800,000 を差し引いて $(152,200)。5年の一時金現価係数 0.62 は使わない撹乱要素である。

questions.stem:
Pole Co. is investing in a machine with a 3-year life. The machine is expected to reduce annual cash operating costs by $30,000 in each of the first 2 years and by $20,000 in Year 3. Present values of an annuity of $1 at 14% are:
Period 1 | 0.88
Period 2 | 1.65
Period 3 | 2.32
Using a 14% cost of capital, what is the present value of these future savings
questions.explanation: The savings are not level, so split them. Years 1-2 at $30,000 use the 2-period annuity factor: $30,000 x 1.65 = $49,500. Year 3's $20,000 needs the 3rd year's factor alone, obtained by subtraction: 2.32 - 1.65 = 0.67, so $20,000 x 0.67 = $13,400. Total = $62,900.
questions.explanationJa: 節約額が毎年一定ではないので分けて計算する。1〜2年目の $30,000 には2期の年金現価係数を使う: $30,000 × 1.65 = $49,500。3年目の $20,000 には3年目単独の係数が必要で、これは差で求める: 2.32 − 1.65 = 0.67。よって $20,000 × 0.67 = $13,400。合計 $62,900。

questions.stem: What is the effect of a stock dividend?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increases the size of the entity

questions.explanation: A stock dividend raises the share count without bringing in any assets, so the same earnings are divided among more shares and future EPS falls. Total equity is unchanged, so the debt-to-equity ratio and the size of the entity are unaffected, and because every holder receives shares in proportion, ownership percentages do not move.
questions.explanationJa: 株式配当は資産の流入を伴わずに発行済株式数を増やすため、同じ利益がより多くの株式に分けられ、将来の1株当たり利益は低下する。資本の総額は変わらないので負債比率も企業規模も影響を受けない。また全株主に持株数に比例して交付されるため、持株比率も動かない。

questions.stem: Yates Company sold $1,000, 7% bonds for $1,250 each. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The market rate of interest is less than 7%.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The market rate of interest is greater than 7%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The market rate of interest equals the coupon rate of interest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bond sells at a discount.

questions.explanation: A bond with a $1,000 face amount selling for $1,250 is trading at a premium. Investors pay more than face only when the 7% coupon exceeds what the market currently demands, so the market rate must be below 7%. A discount price would signal the opposite.
questions.explanationJa: 額面 $1,000 の債券が $1,250 で売れているのはプレミアム発行である。投資家が額面を超えて支払うのは、7%のクーポンが市場が要求する利回りを上回る場合だけなので、市場利子率は7%を下回っていることになる。割引発行ならこの逆を意味する。

questions.stem:
Velocity Company estimates the following for the next year, when common stock is expected to trade at a price-earnings ratio of seven.
Earnings before interest and taxes | $45 million
Interest expense | $5 million
Effective income tax rate | 30%
Preferred stock dividends | $10 million
Common shares outstanding | 2 million
Common stock payout ratio | 25%
What is Velocity's expected common stock dividend for the next year?
questions.explanation: Work down to income available to common: EBIT $45M - interest $5M = $40M pretax; after 30% tax = $28M; less preferred dividends $10M = $18M. EPS = $18M / 2M shares = $9.00. Dividend = $9.00 x 25% payout = $2.25. The price-earnings ratio of seven is not needed for the dividend.
questions.explanationJa: 普通株主に帰属する利益まで順に降ろす。EBIT $45M − 支払利息 $5M = 税引前利益 $40M、30%課税後 $28M、優先株配当 $10M を控除して $18M。1株当たり利益 = $18M ÷ 200万株 = $9.00。配当 = $9.00 × 配当性向25% = $2.25。株価収益率7倍は配当の計算には不要である。

questions.stem: What could a corporation do to decrease the market value per share of common stock?
questions.explanation: A stock dividend increases the number of shares while total value stays the same, so value per share falls. A reverse stock split does the opposite by reducing share count, treasury stock purchases reduce shares outstanding, and retiring bonds on schedule does not change the share count.
questions.explanationJa: 株式配当は発行済株式数を増やす一方で企業の総価値は変わらないため、1株当たりの価値は下がる。株式併合は株式数を減らすので逆の効果、自己株式の取得も流通株式数を減らす。社債の予定どおりの償還は株式数を変えない。

questions.stem: Beam Company currently has 100,000 shares of common stock outstanding and a price-earnings ratio of seven. Net income for the recently ended year is $375,000. Beam's board of directors declared a 15- for-2 stock split. Sunshine owned 100 shares of Beam before the spilt. What is the approximate value of Sunshine's investment in Beam immediately after the split?
questions.explanation: A split changes the number of shares but not the total value of a holding. Before the split: EPS = $375,000 / 100,000 = $3.75, price = $3.75 x 7 = $26.25, and 100 shares are worth $2,625. After the 15-for-2 split the investor holds 750 shares worth $3.50 each, still $2,625.
questions.explanationJa: 株式分割は株式数を変えるが、保有分の総価値は変えない。分割前は 1株当たり利益 = $375,000 ÷ 100,000株 = $3.75、株価 = $3.75 × 7 = $26.25、100株の価値は $2,625。2株を15株にする分割後は750株を保有し1株 $3.50、合計はやはり $2,625 となる。

questions.stem: Why is equity capital generally more expensive than debt financing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dividends fluctuate more than interest rates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interest on bonds is a legal obligation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Investors expect to be paid more for exposure to higher risk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Investors have a greater demand for equity investments than for debt investments.

questions.explanation: Equity holders are paid only after every creditor, and their return depends on residual profits with no promise of payment. Bearing that greater risk, they demand a higher expected return, which makes equity the more expensive source. Interest being a legal obligation (B) is precisely why debt is cheaper, not why equity is expensive.
questions.explanationJa: 株主への分配はすべての債権者への支払いの後であり、その収益は残余利益に依存して支払いの約束もない。この大きなリスクを負う分、株主はより高い期待収益率を要求するため、株主資本の方が高くつく。利息が法的義務であること（B）は、むしろ負債が安い理由であって株主資本が高い理由ではない。

questions.stem:
What ratios are characteristic of an entity with high financial risk?
Debt-to-equity | Interest coverage
questions.explanation: Financial risk comes from the use of debt. A high debt-to-equity ratio shows heavy borrowing, and a low interest coverage ratio shows that earnings barely cover the interest on it. Together they describe an entity with little margin before it cannot service its debt.
questions.explanationJa: 財務リスクは負債の利用から生じる。負債比率が高いことは借入への依存が大きいことを示し、インタレスト・カバレッジ・レシオが低いことは利益が利息をかろうじて賄う水準であることを示す。両者が揃うと、債務を履行できなくなるまでの余裕が乏しい状態を表す。

questions.stem: Which of the following would decrease net working capital?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquiring airplanes using a capital lease with semi-annual payments

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refinancing commercial paper with a 10-year bond issue

questions.explanation: Net working capital is current assets less current liabilities. A capital lease with semi-annual payments adds a current liability for the payments due within a year while the asset acquired is non-current, so working capital falls. Collecting receivables and paying accrued taxes leave the net figure unchanged, and refinancing commercial paper with long-term bonds removes a current liability and increases it.
questions.explanationJa: 正味運転資本は流動資産から流動負債を引いたもの。半年ごとに支払うキャピタルリースは、1年以内に支払う分が流動負債として増える一方、取得する資産は非流動なので運転資本は減少する。売掛金の回収や未払税金の支払いは差引額を変えず、コマーシャルペーパーを長期社債で借り換えると流動負債が減るため運転資本は増加する。

questions.stem: Which of the following ratios would most likely be management to evaluate short-term liquidity?
questions.explanation: The acid test (quick) ratio compares the assets convertible to cash almost immediately with the liabilities coming due, which is the direct measure of short-term liquidity. Return on total assets measures profitability, sales to cash and receivable turnover measure activity rather than the ability to pay.
questions.explanationJa: 当座比率（acid test ratio）は、ほぼ即座に現金化できる資産と、まもなく期限が来る負債とを比べるもので、短期の流動性を直接測る指標である。総資産利益率は収益性、現金回転率や売掛金回転率は活動性を測る指標であり、支払能力そのものを示さない。

questions.stem:
The following table contains Emerald Corp.'s quarterly revenues, in thousands, for the past three years.
During that time, there were no major changes to Emerald's selling strategies and total capital investment.
Year | 1st Qtr. | 2nd Qtr. | 3rd Qtr. | 4th Qtr.
Year 1 | 500 | 500 | 550 | 750
Year 2 | 525 | 550 | 600 | 800
Year 3 | 550 | 525 | 625 | 850
Which of the following statements best describes the likely cause of the fluctuations in Emerald's revenues and the best response to those fluctuations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fluctuations are from changes in the economy, and Emerald should examine its cost structure for potential changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The fluctuations are from changes in the economy, and Emerald should manage its inventories and cash flow to match the cycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fluctuations are from the seasonal demand for Emerald's products, and Emerald should examine its cost structure for potential changes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fluctuations are from the seasonal demand for Emerald's products, and Emerald should manage its inventories and cash flow to match the cycle.

questions.explanation: Every year shows the same shape, with the fourth quarter highest and the first two lowest, and this repeats across three years without changes in strategy or investment. That regularity points to seasonal demand rather than the economy. The right response is to match inventory and cash flow to the cycle; cutting cost structure would not address a pattern that is expected to recur.
questions.explanationJa: 3年とも第4四半期が最も高く第1・2四半期が低いという同じ形を示しており、販売戦略や投資額の変更がないまま繰り返されている。この規則性は景気変動ではなく季節的需要を示す。対応としては在庫とキャッシュフローをその周期に合わせることが適切であり、原価構造の見直しは、繰り返し起こると分かっている変動への対処にはならない。

questions.stem: Green, Inc., a financial investment-consulting firm, was engaged by Maple Corp. to provide technical support for making investment decisions. Maple, a manufacturer of ceramic tiles, was in the process of buying Bay, Inc., its prime competitor. Green's financial analyst made an independent detailed analysis of Bay's average collection period to determine which of following?
questions.explanation: The average collection period measures how long it takes to turn receivables into cash, which speaks to how quickly assets become available to pay obligations. That is a liquidity question. It says nothing directly about how the target is financed, its return to shareholders, or the profitability of its operations.
questions.explanationJa: 平均回収期間は売掛金が現金化するまでの期間を測るもので、資産がどれだけ早く支払いに充てられる形になるかを示す。これは流動性の問題である。買収対象の資金調達構造、株主への収益、事業の収益性を直接示すものではない。

questions.stem: Why would a firm generally choose to finance temporary assets with short-term debt?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Matching the maturities of assets and liabilities reduces risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Short-term interest rates have traditionally been more stable than long-term interest rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: A firm that borrows heavily long term is more apt to be unable to repay the debt than a firm that borrows heavily short term

questions.explanation: Temporary assets, such as a seasonal build-up of inventory, disappear within the year, so financing them with debt that matures in the same period keeps assets and liabilities aligned and avoids paying for financing that is no longer needed. This maturity matching is the standard risk-reducing approach.
questions.explanationJa: 季節的な在庫の積み増しのような一時的資産は1年以内に消滅するため、同じ期間で満期を迎える負債で賄えば資産と負債の期間が対応し、不要になった資金調達に費用を払い続けずに済む。この満期のマッチングがリスクを抑える標準的な考え方である。

questions.stem:
Vie Company is evaluating a plan to expand capacity that will affect the following financial statement amounts.
Current | Plan
Cash | $ 7,000 | $13,000
Marketable securities | $20,000 | $11,000
Accounts receivable | $40,000 | $55,000
Inventory | $38,000 | $48,000
Fixed assets | $70,000 | $90,000
Accounts payable | $35,000 | $44,000
Mortgage payable (current) | $17,000 | $33,000
Mortgage payable (long-term) | $60,000 | $85,000
Retained earnings | $50,000 | $75,000
What is the estimated effect of the expansion on Vie's net working capital?
questions.explanation: Current working capital = ($7,000 + $20,000 + $40,000 + $38,000) - ($35,000 + $17,000) = $105,000 - $52,000 = $53,000. Under the plan = ($13,000 + $11,000 + $55,000 + $48,000) - ($44,000 + $33,000) = $127,000 - $77,000 = $50,000. The change is a decrease of $3,000. Fixed assets, long-term mortgage and retained earnings are excluded because they are not current items.

questions.stem: What of the following is the primary concern of a treasurer managing cash and short-term investments?
questions.explanation: Cash and short-term investments exist to ensure obligations can be met as they come due, so the treasurer's first concern is liquidity. Return, taxes and fees matter only after the ability to pay is secured; chasing yield with funds needed for operations defeats the purpose of holding them.
questions.explanationJa: 現金および短期投資は、支払期日が到来する債務を確実に履行するために保有するものなので、財務担当者の第一の関心は流動性である。収益率・税金・手数料が問題になるのは支払能力を確保した後であり、事業に必要な資金で利回りを追うことは保有目的そのものを損なう。

questions.stem: Griswold Corporation has average ages of inventory, accounts payable, and accounts receivable of 65, 30, and 40, respectively. What is the number of days in the cash flow cycle?
questions.explanation: The cash cycle measures how long cash is tied up: days of inventory plus days of receivables, less the days of credit taken from suppliers. Here 65 + 40 - 30 = 75 days. Adding all three (135) ignores that payables provide financing that shortens the cycle.
questions.explanationJa: キャッシュサイクルは資金が拘束される期間を測る。棚卸資産の日数に売掛金の日数を加え、仕入先から得ている支払猶予の日数を差し引く: 65 + 40 − 30 = 75日。3つを単純に足すと135日となるが、それでは買掛金がサイクルを短縮する資金調達であることを見落としている。

questions.stem: The economic order quantity model may be used for cash management to determine appropriate

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ratio of current assets to current liabilities

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mix of cash and marketable securities

questions.explanation: The economic order quantity model balances the cost of holding an asset against the cost of replenishing it. Applied to cash, holding cost is the interest forgone by not investing, and order cost is the transaction cost of converting securities to cash, so the model determines how to divide funds between cash and marketable securities.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的発注量モデルは、資産を保有する費用と補充する費用のバランスを取るものである。現金に適用すると、保有費用は投資しないことで放棄する利息、発注費用は証券を現金化する取引費用にあたる。したがってこのモデルは、資金を現金と市場性証券にどう配分するかを決める。

questions.stem: A compensating balance is

choices.label: A
choices.text: A quantity of inventory above the economic order quantity held to cover use variation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maintained in an account at a financial institution to cover the cost of services to the account holder

choices.label: C
choices.text: The prepaid interest on a loan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Used to compensate for potential losses on marketable securities used as collateral

questions.explanation: A compensating balance is a minimum balance the borrower agrees to leave on deposit, which the bank uses to cover the cost of servicing the account or the loan. Because those funds cannot be used, the effective cost of the borrowing rises above the stated rate.
questions.explanationJa: コンペンセイティング・バランスとは、借手が預金口座に残しておくことに合意する最低残高であり、銀行はこれを口座や貸付の管理費用の回収に充てる。この資金は使えないため、借入の実効コストは表示金利より高くなる。

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to be used to prepare a cash budget for a manufacturing firm?
questions.explanation: A cash budget tracks money actually received and paid, so it is built from sales and collection patterns, purchases and payment terms. Net income is an accrual figure containing non-cash items such as depreciation and revenue not yet collected, so it is the least useful input.
questions.explanationJa: 現金予算は実際に受け取り支払う資金を追うものなので、売上と回収パターン、仕入、支払条件から組み立てる。純利益は発生主義の数値で、減価償却のような非資金項目や未回収の収益を含むため、現金予算の材料としては最も役に立たない。

questions.stem: Which of the following cash management techniques focuses on cash disbursements?
questions.explanation: A zero-balance account holds no funds until checks presented against it are cleared, at which point exactly enough is transferred from a master account. It is a disbursement technique. Lockboxes, preauthorized checks and depository transfer checks all speed up collections instead.
questions.explanationJa: ゼロ残高口座は、振り出した小切手が呈示されるまで資金を置かず、決済時にちょうど必要な額を親口座から移す仕組みで、支払側の技法である。ロックボックス、事前承認小切手、預金振替小切手はいずれも回収を早める技法であり、支払には関係しない。

questions.stem: A financial manager seeking to delay cash outflows would be most likely to consider using
questions.explanation: A draft is not payable on demand; it must be presented to the drawer for acceptance before funds are released, which buys additional days before cash leaves. Electronic funds transfers and lockboxes accelerate movement of cash, and compensating balances tie funds up rather than delay payment.
questions.explanationJa: ドラフト（手形）は要求払いではなく、振出人に呈示して引受を得るまで資金が出ていかないため、支払までの日数を稼げる。電子資金移動やロックボックスは資金の移動を速める仕組みであり、コンペンセイティング・バランスは資金を拘束するもので支払を遅らせる手段ではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following effects would a lockbox most likely provide for receivables management?
questions.explanation: A lockbox has customers mail payments directly to a post office box serviced by the bank, cutting out mail time to the company and internal processing before deposit. That shortens collection float. Disbursement float concerns the company's own payments and is unaffected.
questions.explanationJa: ロックボックスは、顧客に銀行が管理する私書箱へ直接送金させることで、企業への郵送時間と入金前の社内処理を省く。これにより回収フロートが短縮される。支払フロートは自社の支払いに関する概念であり、ロックボックスの影響を受けない。

questions.stem:
Burrell Company is preparing its cash budget for November. Burrell expects 50% of credit sales to be paid in the month of sale, 30% in the month following the sale, and the remainder paid two months after the month of sale. Burrell expects the following cash and credit sales
Cash | Credit
November | $25,000 | $100,000
October | $20,000 | $90,000
September | $15,000 | $80,000
August | $10,000 | $95,000
Without any bad debts, what is Burrell's expected October cash inflow?
questions.explanation: October collections come from three months of credit sales plus October's cash sales. Credit: October $90,000 x 50% = $45,000, September $80,000 x 30% = $24,000, August $95,000 x 20% = $19,000, totaling $88,000. Adding October cash sales of $20,000 gives $108,000. November's figures are not yet relevant.

questions.stem: Using a 360-day year, what is the current price of a $100 U.S. Treasury bill due in 90 days discounted at a 8% rate?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are sold at a discount from face value. Discount = $100 x 8% x (90 / 360) = $2, so the price today is $100 - $2 = $98. The investor's return is the $2 recovered at maturity.
questions.explanationJa: 米国財務省短期証券は額面から割り引いて売られる。割引額 = $100 × 8% × (90 ÷ 360) = $2 なので、現在価格は $100 − $2 = $98。投資家の収益は満期に回収する $2 である。

questions.stem: Of the following, the marketable security with the least risk is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Commercial paper of an AAA-rated company

choices.label: B
choices.text: Common stock of an AAA-rated company

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stock options of an AAA-rated company

questions.explanation: Commercial paper of a top-rated issuer is a short-term debt obligation with a fixed maturity and a high-quality promise to pay, so both default risk and price volatility are minimal. Common stock and options carry equity price risk, and gold has no issuer promise and fluctuates with commodity markets.
questions.explanationJa: 最上位格付企業のコマーシャルペーパーは満期が確定した短期の債務であり、支払の確実性も高いため、信用リスクも価格変動も最小である。普通株や株式オプションは株価変動リスクを負い、金には発行体の支払約束がなく商品市況で価格が動く。

questions.stem: What is short selling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Selling securities financed by money from a loan that is still outstanding

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selling securities based on inside information

choices.label: C
choices.text: Selling securities that are not owned by the seller

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speculating that securities will have a dramatic price increase

questions.explanation: Short selling means selling securities the seller does not own, typically borrowing them to deliver and buying them back later. The seller profits if the price falls, which is the opposite of the expectation described in choice D.
questions.explanationJa: 空売りとは、売手が保有していない証券を売ることであり、通常は借りて受け渡し、後に買い戻す。価格が下落すれば利益となるため、選択肢Dが述べる値上がりの期待とは正反対の取引である。

questions.stem: Short-term notes issued by Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) are called
questions.explanation: Fannie Mae is a government-sponsored enterprise, and the short-term obligations it issues are known as agency securities. Bankers' acceptances arise from trade financing, municipal bonds are issued by state and local governments, and repurchase agreements are collateralized borrowing transactions.
questions.explanationJa: ファニーメイは政府支援機関であり、同機関が発行する短期債務はエージェンシー証券と呼ばれる。銀行引受手形は貿易金融から生じるもの、地方債は州・地方政府が発行するもの、レポ取引は担保付きの資金借入取引である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is most often used as a cash substitute?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills combine no default risk with a deep secondary market, so they can be turned into cash immediately at a predictable price. That is what makes them the standard cash substitute. The other instruments carry more credit or liquidity risk.
questions.explanationJa: 米国財務省短期証券は信用リスクがないうえ流通市場に厚みがあり、予測可能な価格で即座に現金化できる。この性質が現金代替として標準的に使われる理由である。他の商品は信用リスクか流動性リスクがより大きい。

questions.stem: Commercial paper's advantages include that it

choices.label: A
choices.text: Can be purchased without commission costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is readily available as a financing source to most businesses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provides a line of credit at a preset fixed rate that can be used as needed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Typically is cheaper than a commercial bank loan

questions.explanation: Commercial paper is unsecured short-term debt sold directly to investors, bypassing the bank's intermediation margin, so it usually costs less than a bank loan. It is available only to large, highly rated issuers, is bought and sold with dealer spreads, and is not a committed line of credit.
questions.explanationJa: コマーシャルペーパーは投資家に直接販売される無担保の短期債務で、銀行の仲介マージンを迂回するため、通常は銀行借入より調達コストが低い。ただし利用できるのは格付の高い大企業に限られ、売買にはディーラーのスプレッドが伴い、また随時引き出せる与信枠でもない。

questions.stem: What is the average collection period?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average number of days before a receivable account becomes delinquent

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average number of days from a credit sale to payment receipt

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average number of days from inventory purchase to sale

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average number of days from the time a customer issues a check to the time the vendor receives use of the funds

questions.explanation: The average collection period is days sales outstanding: how long, on average, from making a credit sale to receiving the cash. Choice C describes the inventory conversion period, and D describes float rather than the collection period.
questions.explanationJa: 平均回収期間は売掛金回転日数であり、信用売上を行ってから現金を受け取るまでの平均日数を指す。選択肢Cは棚卸資産の回転期間、Dは回収期間ではなくフロートの説明である。

questions.stem: Jones Wholesaling has average daily sales of $50,000, based on a 360-day year. All of Jones's sales are on credit with terms of 2/10, net 45. Customers representing 30% of sales pay on day 45 and the remaining customers take the discount and pay on day 10. What are Jones' average daily collections from customers?
questions.explanation: Split the collections by behaviour. The 70% who take the discount remit only 98%: $50,000 x 70% x 98% = $34,300. The 30% who wait until day 45 pay in full: $50,000 x 30% = $15,000. Average daily collections = $49,300. The $700 difference from $50,000 is the cost of the discounts.
questions.explanationJa: 顧客の行動別に分けて計算する。割引を利用する70%は98%しか支払わない: $50,000 × 70% × 98% = $34,300。45日目に支払う30%は満額を支払う: $50,000 × 30% = $15,000。平均日次回収額 = $49,300。$50,000 との差 $700 が割引の負担分である。

questions.stem: Innovate Corporation changed its credit policy. The result is increased sales, increased discounts taken, reduced accounts receivable, and reduced doubtful accounts. Which of the following is also true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average collection period is reduced.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bad debt loss percentage increased.

questions.explanation: Lower receivables alongside higher sales can only happen if customers are paying faster, and more discounts being taken confirms it. Faster payment shortens the average collection period. Falling doubtful accounts means the bad debt percentage went down, not up, and nothing indicates a smaller discount or lower gross profit.
questions.explanationJa: 売上が増えているのに売掛金が減るのは、顧客の支払いが早くなった場合に限られ、割引の利用が増えている事実がそれを裏づける。支払いが早まれば平均回収期間は短縮される。貸倒引当が減っているので貸倒率は上昇ではなく低下しており、割引率の縮小や売上総利益の減少を示す材料もない。

questions.stem:
A company has the following information in its financial records:
Beginning balance | Ending balance
Cash | $3,900 | $3,000
Marketable securities | 3,800 | 4,400
Accounts receivable | 14,600 | 12,900
Total current assets | $22,300 | $20,300
Net sales | $103,200
Expenses | 20,430
Net income | $82,770
What is the company's receivable turnover ratio?
questions.explanation: Receivable turnover = net sales / average accounts receivable. Average receivables = ($14,600 + $12,900) / 2 = $13,750. Turnover = $103,200 / $13,750 = 7.5. Using the ending balance alone would give 8.0 (choice D).
questions.explanationJa: 売掛金回転率 = 純売上高 ÷ 平均売掛金。平均売掛金 = ($14,600 + $12,900) ÷ 2 = $13,750。回転率 = $103,200 ÷ $13,750 = 7.5。期末残高だけで計算すると 8.0（選択肢D）となり誤る。

questions.stem: The CFO of a company is concerned about the company's accounts receivable turnover ratio. The company currently offers customers terms of 3/10, net 30. Which of the following strategies would most likely improve the company's accounts receivable turnover ratio?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pledging the accounts receivable to a finance company

choices.label: C
choices.text: Entering into a factoring agreement with a finance company

questions.explanation: Extending the discount period from 10 to 20 days while keeping the 3% discount gives customers who were paying on day 30 a reason to pay on day 20 instead, pulling cash in sooner and raising turnover. Cutting the discount to 1% (B) weakens the incentive. Pledging receivables (A) does not change when customers pay, and factoring (C) sells the receivables rather than improving collection behaviour.
questions.explanationJa: 割引率3%を維持したまま割引期間を10日から20日へ延ばすと、30日目に支払っていた顧客が20日目に支払う誘因が生まれ、資金の回収が早まって回転率が上がる。割引率を1%に下げる（B）と誘因が弱まる。売掛金の担保差入（A）は顧客の支払時期を変えず、ファクタリング（C）は売掛金を売却するもので回収行動そのものの改善ではない。

questions.stem: Super Sets, Inc. manufactures and sells television sets. AII sales are finalized on credit with terms of 2/10, n/30. Seventy percent of Super Set customers take discounts and pay on day 10, while the remaining 30% pay on day 30. What is the average collection period in days?
questions.explanation: Weight each group by the days it takes: 70% x 10 days = 7, plus 30% x 30 days = 9, giving an average of 16 days. Answering 10 or 30 uses only one group, and 40 simply adds the two payment dates.
questions.explanationJa: 各グループを支払日数で加重平均する: 70% × 10日 = 7、30% × 30日 = 9、合計16日。10日や30日はどちらか一方のグループしか見ておらず、40日は2つの支払日を単に足しただけの誤り。

questions.stem: Stellar Company is considering a change in collection procedures that would result in an increase of the average collection period from 28 to 36 days. Stellar estimates next year's sales to be $9 million and that 80% of sales will be on credit. Stellar estimates short-term investment rates at 6% and uses a 360 day year for decision making. What minimum savings in collection costs would the procedure change have to generate to offset the increased investment in accounts receivable?
questions.explanation: Refer to the video explanation in the Proactive question bank (BAR CH51, Q.42, code 7308).
questions.explanationJa: 解説はProactive過去問解説の動画を参照（BAR CH51 / Q.42 / コード 7308）。

questions.stem: Revel Company has average daily sales of $5,000, 90% of which are on credit. Receivables are collected 28 days after sales, on average. What is Revel's average accounts receivable balance?
questions.explanation: Average receivables = daily credit sales x days outstanding. Daily credit sales = $5,000 x 90% = $4,500, so the balance = $4,500 x 28 = $126,000. Using total sales of $5,000 instead would give $140,000 (choice D), which ignores that 10% of sales are for cash.
questions.explanationJa: 平均売掛金 = 日次信用売上 × 回収日数。日次信用売上 = $5,000 × 90% = $4,500 なので、残高 = $4,500 × 28日 = $126,000。総売上 $5,000 で計算すると $140,000（選択肢D）となるが、それでは売上の10%が現金売上である点を無視することになる。

questions.stem: Green Co. has an inventory conversion period of 80 days and annual revenue of $4,200,000. How many times per year (360 days) does Green turn over its inventory?
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover and the conversion period are reciprocals scaled by the year: turnover = 360 / 80 days = 4.5 times. The revenue figure is not needed; it is there to tempt a cost-of-sales style calculation that the question does not support.
questions.explanationJa: 棚卸資産回転率と回転期間は、年間日数を介して互いに逆数の関係にある: 回転率 = 360日 ÷ 80日 = 4.5回。売上高の数値は不要であり、売上原価を用いる計算に誘導するための撹乱要素である。

questions.stem: When would a retailer tend to decrease the safety stock of inventory?
questions.explanation: Safety stock is insurance against running out, and its price is the cost of holding it. When carrying cost rises, that insurance becomes more expensive and the retailer holds less. Greater sales variability, higher volume and longer transportation time all make stockouts more likely and argue for more safety stock.
questions.explanationJa: 安全在庫は品切れに対する保険であり、その対価が保有コストである。保有コストが上昇すればこの保険が割高になるため、小売業者は安全在庫を減らす。売上の変動が大きくなること、販売量が増えること、輸送日数が延びることは、いずれも品切れの可能性を高めるため安全在庫を増やす方向に働く。

questions.stem:
In Belk Co.'s "just-in-time" production system, costs per setup were reduced from $28 to $2. In the process of reducing inventory levels, Belk found that there were fixed facility and administrative costs that previously had not been included in the carrying cost calculation. The result was an increase from $8 to $32 per unit per year. What were the effects of these changes on Belk's economic lot size and relevant costs?
Lot size | Relevant costs
questions.explanation: Economic lot size is the square root of (2 x demand x setup cost / carrying cost). Setup cost fell from $28 to $2 while carrying cost rose from $8 to $32, so the numerator shrank and the denominator grew: lot size falls sharply. Total relevant cost is the square root of (2 x demand x setup x carrying), and 2 x 32 = 64 is well below 28 x 8 = 224, so relevant costs fall as well.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的ロットサイズは √(2 × 需要 × 段取費用 ÷ 保有費用) で表される。段取費用が $28 から $2 へ下がり、保有費用が $8 から $32 へ上がったため、分子は縮小し分母は拡大してロットサイズは大きく減少する。関連原価の総額は √(2 × 需要 × 段取費用 × 保有費用) であり、2 × 32 = 64 は 28 × 8 = 224 を大きく下回るので、関連原価も減少する。

questions.stem: What costs are included in ordering costs in the economic order quantity model?
questions.explanation: Ordering costs are incurred each time an order is placed, and buying in smaller lots forfeits quantity discounts, so that lost discount is an ordering-related cost. Handling, insurance and interest on capital tied up all accrue while the goods sit in stock, making them carrying costs.
questions.explanationJa: 発注コストは発注のたびに発生する費用であり、小口で発注すると数量割引を逃すため、この逸失分は発注に関連する費用となる。荷役費、保険料、拘束資本にかかる利息は、いずれも在庫が保管されている間に発生するので保有コストにあたる。

questions.stem: The economic order quantity model indicates the
questions.explanation: The economic order quantity is the size of a single order that minimises the sum of ordering and carrying costs. It says nothing directly about annual quantities; average inventory is EOQ divided by two plus any safety stock.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的発注量は、発注コストと保有コストの合計を最小にする「1回あたり」の発注数量である。年間の数量を直接示すものではない。平均在庫はEOQを2で割り、安全在庫があればそれを加えた値になる。

questions.stem: What costs are not included in carrying costs in the economic order quantity model?
questions.explanation: Carrying costs accrue while inventory is held: handling, insurance, and interest on the capital tied up. Shipping is incurred in bringing the goods in and belongs with ordering costs, which is why it is the exception here.
questions.explanationJa: 保有コストは在庫を保管している間に発生する費用で、荷役費・保険料・拘束資本の利息が該当する。輸送費は商品を入荷させる際に発生するもので発注コストに属するため、保有コストに含まれない例外となる。

questions.stem: An increase in which of the following should cause management to reduce the average inventory?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cost of placing an order

choices.label: C
choices.text: The annual demand for the product

choices.label: D
choices.text: The lead time needed to acquire inventory

questions.explanation: Higher carrying cost sits in the denominator of the EOQ formula, so the optimal order quantity falls and with it the average inventory. Higher ordering cost or higher annual demand would increase EOQ, and longer lead time affects the reorder point rather than the order size.
questions.explanationJa: 保有コストの上昇はEOQ計算式の分母に入るため、最適発注量が減り、それに伴って平均在庫も減少する。発注コストの上昇や年間需要の増加はEOQを増やす方向に働き、リードタイムの長期化は発注量ではなく再発注点に影響する。

questions.stem: Mystery Company uses the economic order quantity model to determine order size. Mystery's order quantity for Product XYZ is 150 units. Mystery has a safety stock of 50 units for Product XYZ. What is Mystery's average inventory level for Product XYZ?
questions.explanation: Order quantities are drawn down to the safety stock and then replenished, so on average half an order is on hand plus the safety stock throughout: 150 / 2 + 50 = 125 units. Ignoring the safety stock gives 75, and adding the full order quantity gives 200.
questions.explanationJa: 発注量は安全在庫の水準まで消費されてから補充されるため、平均すると発注量の半分に安全在庫を加えた量が常時手元にあることになる: 150 ÷ 2 + 50 = 125単位。安全在庫を無視すると75、発注量をそのまま足すと200となり誤る。

questions.stem:
In computing the reorder point for an item of inventory, which of the following is used?
I. Cost
II. Usage per day III. Lead time
questions.explanation: The reorder point marks the stock level at which a new order must be placed so that it arrives before stock runs out, which requires only how fast inventory is consumed and how long delivery takes: usage per day times lead time. Cost affects how much to order, not when.
questions.explanationJa: 再発注点は、在庫が尽きる前に納品が間に合うよう発注をかけるべき在庫水準を示すもので、必要なのは在庫が消費される速さと納品までの日数だけである（1日使用量 × リードタイム）。コストは「いくら発注するか」に影響する要素であって、「いつ発注するか」には関係しない。

questions.stem: Unity Company has made changes in its inventory handling policies that are expected to increase turnover from 7 to 8 times per year. Unity's budgeted sales and costs of sales for the next year are $42 million and $28 million, respectively. At a 6% interest rate, what are Unity's expected savings from the lower inventory level?
questions.explanation: Average inventory = cost of sales / turnover. At 7 turns: $28,000,000 / 7 = $4,000,000. At 8 turns: $28,000,000 / 8 = $3,500,000. The $500,000 released earns 6%, saving $30,000. Sales of $42 million are not used because inventory is carried at cost.
questions.explanationJa: 平均在庫 = 売上原価 ÷ 回転率。回転率7回では $28,000,000 ÷ 7 = $4,000,000、8回では $28,000,000 ÷ 8 = $3,500,000。解放される $500,000 が6%で運用され、節約額は $30,000。在庫は原価で計上されるため、売上高 $42 million は使わない。

questions.stem:
A corporation manages inventory performance by monitoring its inventory turnover. Selected financial records for the corporation are as follows:
Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3
Annual sales | $1,262,500 | $1,062,500 | $1,459,000
Gross annual profit percentage | 45% | 30% | 40%
The beginning finished goods inventory for year 2 was 20% of year 2 sales. The ending finished goods inventory for year 2 was 18% of year 3 sales. What was the corporation's inventory turnover for year 2?
questions.explanation: Cost of sales for year 2 = $1,062,500 x (1 - 30%) = $743,750. Beginning inventory = 20% of year 2 sales = $212,500; ending inventory = 18% of year 3 sales = $1,459,000 x 18% = $262,620. Average = $237,560. Turnover = $743,750 / $237,560 = 3.13. Note the ending balance is tied to year 3 sales, not year 2.

questions.stem: Level Company's current ratio is 2.5 to 1. Level's current liabilities are $252,000. Loan provisions require that Level's current ratio not drop below 1.5 to 1. What is the maximum additional short-term debt that Level may incur?
questions.explanation: Current assets = 2.5 x $252,000 = $630,000. The covenant requires current assets / current liabilities to stay at or above 1.5. Additional short-term debt that does not itself add a current asset gives $630,000 / ($252,000 + X) = 1.5, so $252,000 = 1.5X - $378,000 + $378,000, giving X = $168,000. If the borrowing also raised cash, the limit would be far higher, so the question assumes the proceeds do not remain in current assets.
questions.explanationJa: 流動資産 = 2.5 × $252,000 = $630,000。財務制限条項は流動比率を1.5以上に保つことを求める。流動資産を増やさない形で短期債務を追加する場合、$630,000 ÷ ($252,000 + X) = 1.5 となり、X = $168,000。もし借入で現金が増えるなら限度額はもっと大きくなるため、設問は調達した資金が流動資産として残らない前提を置いている。

questions.stem: A company has an outstanding one-year bank loan of $500,000 at a stated interest rate of 8%. The company is required to maintain a 20% compensating balance in its checking account. The company would maintain a zero balance in this account if the requirement did not exist. What is the effective interest rate of the loan?
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the full $500,000: $40,000. The 20% compensating balance locks up $100,000, so only $400,000 is actually usable. Effective rate = $40,000 / $400,000 = 10%. The compensating balance raises the true cost precisely because the borrower pays for funds it cannot use.
questions.explanationJa: 利息は借入額 $500,000 全額に課される: $40,000。20%のコンペンセイティング・バランスにより $100,000 が拘束されるため、実際に使えるのは $400,000。実効金利 = $40,000 ÷ $400,000 = 10%。使えない資金にも利息を払うことが、実質的なコストを押し上げる理由である。

questions.stem: What is called a spontaneous financing source?
questions.explanation: Trade credit arises automatically as the company buys on account; no negotiation or formal agreement is needed and it grows and shrinks with purchases. Mortgages, debentures and notes payable all require deliberate arrangement, so they are negotiated rather than spontaneous.
questions.explanationJa: 企業間信用（買掛金）は掛けで仕入れれば自動的に生じ、交渉も正式な契約も要さず、仕入の増減に応じて自然に増減する。動産抵当・社債・支払手形はいずれも意図的な取り決めを必要とするため、自然発生的ではなく交渉によって得る資金調達である。

questions.stem: Quail Company's suppliers offer terms of 2/10, net 35. Using a 360-day year, what is the approximate cost of foregoing the discount?
questions.explanation: Cost of forgoing the discount = discount / (100% - discount) x 360 / (net days - discount days) = 2 / 98 x 360 / (35 - 10) = 0.0204 x 14.4 = about 29%. The denominator uses the 25 extra days of credit actually gained by not taking the discount.
questions.explanationJa: 割引を見送るコスト = 割引率 ÷ (100% − 割引率) × 360 ÷ (支払期日 − 割引期限) = 2 ÷ 98 × 360 ÷ (35 − 10) = 0.0204 × 14.4 ≒ 29%。分母には、割引を放棄することで実際に得られる25日分の追加与信期間を用いる。

questions.stem: Which of the following is secured debt?
questions.explanation: Factoring involves specific receivables being assigned or sold to the lender, so particular assets stand behind the financing. Commercial paper is unsecured by definition, and lines of credit and revolving credit are general borrowing arrangements that ordinarily carry no pledged collateral.
questions.explanationJa: ファクタリングでは特定の売掛金が金融機関に譲渡または売却されるため、個別の資産が資金調達の裏付けとなる。コマーシャルペーパーは定義上無担保であり、与信枠やリボルビング・クレジットは一般的な借入枠であって通常は担保を差し入れない。

questions.stem: What is the prime rate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The rate that a bank charges its strongest commercial customers

choices.label: C
choices.text: The rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans for funds to meet minimal reserve requirements

choices.label: D
choices.text: The rate that the Federal Reserve charges banks for funds

questions.explanation: The prime rate is the rate a bank quotes to its most creditworthy commercial borrowers and serves as a benchmark for other loans. Choice C describes the federal funds rate and D the discount rate charged by the Federal Reserve.
questions.explanationJa: プライムレートは、銀行が最も信用力の高い法人顧客に提示する金利であり、他の貸付の基準として使われる。選択肢Cはフェデラルファンドレート、Dは連邦準備制度が銀行に課す公定歩合の説明である。

questions.stem: A small retail business most likely would finance merchandise inventory with
questions.explanation: A line of credit lets a small retailer draw funds as inventory is bought and repay as it sells, matching the financing to a fluctuating need. Commercial paper is available only to large highly rated issuers, a chattel mortgage is used for equipment, and factoring finances receivables rather than inventory.
questions.explanationJa: 与信枠なら、小規模小売業者は在庫を仕入れる際に資金を引き出し、販売に応じて返済でき、変動する資金需要に調達を合わせられる。コマーシャルペーパーは格付の高い大企業しか利用できず、動産抵当は設備を対象とし、ファクタリングは在庫ではなく売掛金を資金化する手段である。

questions.stem:
Oak Company bought a machine which they will depreciate on the straight-line basis over an estimated useful life of seven years. The machine has no salvage value. They expect the machine to generate after-tax net cash inflows from operations of $110,000 in each of the seven years. Oak's minimum rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows:
- Present value of $1 at 12% at the end of seven periods | 0.0452
- Present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 at 12% for seven periods | 4.564
Assuming a positive net present value of $12,000, what was the cost of the machine?
questions.explanation: Net present value = present value of inflows - cost, so cost = present value of inflows - NPV. PV of inflows = $110,000 x 4.564 (the ordinary annuity factor) = $502,040. Cost = $502,040 - $12,000 = $490,040. The single-sum factor 0.0452 is not used because the cash flows are an annuity.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値 = 流入の現在価値 − 取得原価。したがって 取得原価 = 流入の現在価値 − NPV。流入の現在価値 = $110,000 × 4.564（年金現価係数）= $502,040。取得原価 = $502,040 − $12,000 = $490,040。キャッシュフローが年金形式なので、一時金の現価係数 0.0452 は使わない。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the payback method as a capital budgeting technique?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The payback method considers the time value of money.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An advantage of the payback method is that it indicates if an investment will be profitable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The payback method provides the years needed to recoup the investment in a project.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Payback is calculated by dividing the annual cash inflows by the net investment.

questions.explanation: The payback period is simply the time needed to recover the original investment. It does not discount, so A is wrong; recovering the outlay says nothing about profitability over the whole life, so B is wrong; and the formula is investment divided by annual cash inflow, the reverse of D.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間は当初投資額を回収するのに要する期間そのものを示す。割引計算を行わないためAは誤り。投資額の回収は全期間の収益性を語らないためBも誤り。計算式は「投資額 ÷ 年間キャッシュフロー」であり、Dは分子と分母が逆。

questions.stem: Net present value as used in investment decision-making is stated in terms of which of the following options?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Earnings before interest, taxes, and depreciation

questions.explanation: Net present value discounts CASH FLOWS, not accounting income. Net income and the various earnings measures include non-cash items such as depreciation and follow accrual timing, so they do not represent the amounts available for discounting.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値が割り引くのは「キャッシュフロー」であり会計上の利益ではない。純利益や各種の利益指標は減価償却などの非資金項目を含み、発生主義のタイミングに従うため、割引の対象となる金額を表さない。

questions.stem: What is the formula for calculating the profitability index of a project?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Subtract actual after-tax net income from the minimum required return in dollars

choices.label: B
choices.text: Divide the present value of the annual after-tax cash flows by the original cash invested in the project

choices.label: C
choices.text: Divide the initial investment for the project by the net annual cash inflow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Multiply net profit margin by asset turnover

questions.explanation: The profitability index expresses value created per dollar invested: present value of the after-tax cash flows divided by the initial investment. An index above 1.0 corresponds to a positive net present value. Choice C is the payback formula, and D is the DuPont decomposition of return on assets.
questions.explanationJa: 収益性指数は投資1ドルあたりどれだけの価値を生むかを表し、税引後キャッシュフローの現在価値 ÷ 当初投資額で求める。指数が1.0を超えることは正味現在価値がプラスであることと対応する。選択肢Cは回収期間の式、Dはデュポン分解による総資産利益率の式である。

questions.stem:
A project has an initial outlay of $1,000. The projected cash inflows are:
Year 1 | $200
Year 2 | 200
Year 3 | 400
Year 4 | 400
What is the investment's payback period?
questions.explanation: Cumulative inflows: year 1 $200, year 2 $400, year 3 $800. After three years $200 of the $1,000 outlay remains, and year 4 brings in $400, so $200 / $400 = 0.5 of a year is needed. Payback = 3.5 years.
questions.explanationJa: 累計流入額は1年目 $200、2年目 $400、3年目 $800。3年経過時点で投資額 $1,000 のうち $200 が未回収。4年目の流入は $400 なので $200 ÷ $400 = 0.5年で回収できる。回収期間 = 3.5年。

questions.stem:
The target capital structure of Traggle Co. is 50% debt, 10% preferred equity, and 40% common equity.
The interest rate on debt is 6%, the yield on the preferred is 7%, the cost of common equity is 11.5%, and the tax rate is 40%. Traggle does not anticipate issuing any new stock. What is Traggle's weighted- average cost of capital?
questions.explanation: Only debt gives a tax deduction, so its cost is 6% x (1 - 40%) = 3.6%. Weighted: debt 50% x 3.6% = 1.8%, preferred 10% x 7% = 0.7%, common 40% x 11.5% = 4.6%. Total = 7.1%. Preferred dividends are not deductible, so the 7% is not tax-adjusted.
questions.explanationJa: 節税効果があるのは負債だけなので、その資本コストは 6% × (1 − 40%) = 3.6%。加重すると、負債 50% × 3.6% = 1.8%、優先株 10% × 7% = 0.7%、普通株 40% × 11.5% = 4.6%。合計 7.1%。優先株配当は損金にならないため、7%に税調整は行わない。

questions.stem: What is the primary disadvantage of using return on investment (ROI) rather than residual income (RI) to evaluate the performance of investment center managers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ROI is a percentage, while RI is a dollar amount.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ROI may lead to rejecting projects that yield positive cash flows.

choices.label: C
choices.text: ROI does not necessarily reflect the company's cost of capital.

choices.label: D
choices.text: ROI does not reflect all economic gains.

questions.explanation: A manager judged on ROI will refuse a project that earns less than the division's current ROI even when it exceeds the company's cost of capital and would add value. Residual income avoids this because any return above the capital charge increases it. The other statements are true of ROI but are not the reason it distorts decisions.
questions.explanationJa: ROIで評価される管理者は、全社の資本コストを上回り企業価値を高めるプロジェクトであっても、自部門の現在のROIを下回るなら採用を拒む。残余利益ではこの歪みが生じない。資本費用を上回る収益であれば必ず残余利益が増えるためである。他の記述もROIの性質としては正しいが、意思決定を歪める理由そのものではない。

questions.stem:
SkBound Airlines provided the following information about its two operating divisions:
Passenger | Cargo
Operating profit | $ 40,000 | $ 50,000
Investment | $250,000 | $500,000
External borrowing rate | 6% | 8%
Measuring performance using return on investment (ROI), which division performed better?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Cargo division, with an ROI of 10%

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Passenger division, with an ROI of 16%

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Cargo division, with an ROI of 18%

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Passenger division, with an ROI of 22%

questions.explanation: Return on investment = operating profit / investment. Passenger = $40,000 / $250,000 = 16%; Cargo = $50,000 / $500,000 = 10%. Passenger performs better despite earning less in absolute dollars, because it uses far less capital. The borrowing rates are not part of the ROI calculation.
questions.explanationJa: 投下資本利益率 = 営業利益 ÷ 投資額。旅客部門 = $40,000 ÷ $250,000 = 16%、貨物部門 = $50,000 ÷ $500,000 = 10%。金額では貨物部門が上回るが、旅客部門ははるかに少ない資本で稼いでいるため業績は旅客部門の方が良い。借入金利はROIの計算には入らない。

questions.stem:
The following selected data pertain to the Darwin Division of Beagle Co. for Year 1.
Sales | $400,000
Operating income | 40,000
Capital turnover | 4
Imputed interest rate | 10%
What was Darwin's Year 1 residual income?
questions.explanation: Capital turnover of 4 means invested capital = sales / 4 = $400,000 / 4 = $100,000. Residual income = operating income - (investment x imputed rate) = $40,000 - ($100,000 x 10%) = $30,000. The imputed interest is a charge for the capital used, not a cash cost.
questions.explanationJa: 資本回転率4は、投下資本 = 売上 ÷ 4 = $400,000 ÷ 4 = $100,000 であることを意味する。残余利益 = 営業利益 − (投資額 × 帰属利子率) = $40,000 − ($100,000 × 10%) = $30,000。帰属利子は使用した資本に対する賦課であり、実際に支払う費用ではない。

questions.stem:
Wexford Co. has a subunit that reported the following data for year 1:
Asset (investment) turnover | 1.5 times
Sales | $750,000
Return on sales | 8%
The imputed interest rate is 12%. What is the division residual income for year 1?
questions.explanation: Investment = sales / asset turnover = $750,000 / 1.5 = $500,000. Operating income = sales x return on sales = $750,000 x 8% = $60,000. Capital charge = $500,000 x 12% = $60,000. Residual income = $60,000 - $60,000 = $0, meaning the subunit earned exactly its required return and created no surplus.
questions.explanationJa: 投資額 = 売上 ÷ 資産回転率 = $750,000 ÷ 1.5 = $500,000。営業利益 = 売上 × 売上高利益率 = $750,000 × 8% = $60,000。資本費用 = $500,000 × 12% = $60,000。残余利益 = $60,000 − $60,000 = $0。すなわちこの部門は要求収益をちょうど達成しただけで、上乗せの価値は生んでいない。

questions.stem: How do short-term interest rates compare to long-term interest rates?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Short-term rates are lower than long-term rates during periods of high inflation

questions.explanation: Under a normal upward-sloping yield curve, lenders demand more for tying up funds longer, so short-term rates sit below long-term rates. The relationship inverts only in unusual conditions, which is why the general answer is that short rates are lower.
questions.explanationJa: 通常の右上がりのイールドカーブの下では、資金を長く拘束されることへの対価が求められるため、短期金利は長期金利より低くなる。この関係が逆転するのは特異な局面に限られるので、一般論としては短期金利の方が低いとなる。

questions.stem: What is an underwriting spread?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Commission that an investment banker earns for underwriting a security issue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Difference between the price that an investment banker pays for a security and the price that a subsequent investor pays for the security

choices.label: C
choices.text: Discount that an investment banker receives on a security issue

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fee that an investment banker receives to prepare, print, and distribute a security issue

questions.explanation: The underwriter buys the issue from the company at one price and resells it to investors at a higher one. That difference is the underwriting spread and is how the investment bank is compensated, rather than through a separately billed commission or preparation fee.
questions.explanationJa: 引受業者は発行会社から証券をある価格で買い取り、投資家にはより高い価格で転売する。この差額がアンダーライティング・スプレッドであり、投資銀行の報酬はこの形で得られる。別途請求する手数料や資料作成費として受け取るものではない。

questions.stem:
Carmen Company has the following equity amounts and no dividends in arrears.
Preferred stock, $1,000 par | $24 million
Common stock, $100 par | $20 million
Paid-in capital in excess of par | $36 million
Retained earnings | $18 million
What is the book value of Carmen's common stock?
questions.explanation: Total equity = $24M + $20M + $36M + $18M = $98M. Remove the preferred claim of $24M (no dividends are in arrears), leaving $74M for common. Shares = $20M / $100 par = 200,000. Book value per share = $74M / 200,000 = $370.
questions.explanationJa: 株主資本合計 = $24M + $20M + $36M + $18M = $98M。優先株の請求権 $24M を控除すると（配当の延滞はない）、普通株に帰属するのは $74M。普通株式数 = $20M ÷ 額面 $100 = 200,000株。1株当たり簿価 = $74M ÷ 200,000株 = $370。

questions.stem:
Carmen Company has the following equity amounts and no dividends in arrears.
Preferred stock, $1,000 par | $24 million
Common stock, $100 par | $20 million
Paid-in capital in excess of par | $36 million
Retained earnings | $18 million
Diego owns 1,000 shares of Carmen. If Carmen Company issues an additional 100,000 shares of common stock, how many additional shares does Diego have the opportunity to buy?
questions.explanation: A preemptive right lets a holder maintain the same ownership percentage. Diego holds 1,000 of 200,000 shares, or 0.5%, so of the 100,000 new shares he may buy 0.5% x 100,000 = 500 shares.
questions.explanationJa: 新株引受権により、株主は持株比率を維持できる。Diegoは 200,000株のうち 1,000株、すなわち 0.5% を保有しているので、新規発行 100,000株のうち 0.5% × 100,000 = 500株を購入できる。

questions.stem: Which of the following ratios would be used to evaluate a company's profitability?
questions.explanation: Gross margin ratio measures how much profit remains from each sales dollar, which is a profitability measure. The current ratio measures liquidity, inventory turnover measures activity or efficiency, and debt to total assets measures solvency.
questions.explanationJa: 売上総利益率は売上1ドルあたりどれだけ利益が残るかを測る収益性の指標である。流動比率は流動性、棚卸資産回転率は活動性（効率性）、負債比率は安全性（支払能力）を測る指標であり、いずれも収益性の指標ではない。

questions.stem: To maximize shareholder wealth, which of the following measures is most appropriate for management focus?
questions.explanation: Shareholder wealth comes from both dividends received and the change in share price, and total return per share captures both. Earnings per share and profits are accounting figures that ignore risk and timing, and stock value alone omits the dividends already paid out.
questions.explanationJa: 株主の富は受け取る配当と株価の変動の両方から生じ、1株当たり総収益はその両方を捉える。1株当たり利益や利益額はリスクとタイミングを無視した会計上の数値であり、株価だけでは既に支払われた配当が抜け落ちる。

questions.stem:
Mott Company has a $100 ten-year, 6% certificate of deposit that receives interest annually. Present and future value factors are as follows:
Present value of 1 at 6% for 10 periods | 0.614
Future value of 1 at 6% for 10 periods | 1.791
Present value of ordinary annuity of 1 at 6% for 10 periods | 7.360
Future value of ordinary annuity of 1 at 6% for 10 periods | 13.181
How much will Mott Co. receive in ten years?
questions.explanation: The $100 principal compounds for ten years, so use the future value of 1: $100 x 1.791 = $179. The annuity factors would apply only if $100 were deposited every year, and the present value factors move in the wrong direction.
questions.explanationJa: 元本 $100 が10年間複利で増えるので、一時金の終価係数を使う: $100 × 1.791 = $179。年金の係数は毎年 $100 ずつ預け入れる場合にのみ使うものであり、現価係数は時間の向きが逆である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of net present value modeling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is measured in time, not dollars.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It uses accrual basis, not cash basis accounting for a project.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It uses the accounting rate of return.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It accounts for compounding of returns.

questions.explanation: Discounting each future cash flow back to today embeds compounding: a dollar received later is worth less precisely because the earlier dollar could have been reinvested. NPV is stated in dollars, uses cash flows rather than accruals, and is unrelated to the accounting rate of return.
questions.explanationJa: 将来の各キャッシュフローを現在に割り引く手続きには複利の考え方が組み込まれている。後に受け取る1ドルの価値が低いのは、早く受け取れば再投資できたからである。NPVは金額で表され、発生主義ではなくキャッシュフローを用い、会計的利益率とは無関係である。

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is inherent in a firm's operations if it utilizes only equity financing?
questions.explanation: Business risk is the variability in operating results caused by the nature of the firm's operations, and it exists regardless of how the firm is financed. Financial risk arises only from the use of debt, so a firm funded entirely by equity carries business risk alone.
questions.explanationJa: 事業リスクは事業の性質そのものから生じる営業成績の変動であり、資金調達の方法にかかわらず存在する。財務リスクは負債の利用によってのみ生じるため、株主資本だけで調達している企業が負うのは事業リスクだけとなる。

questions.stem: An appropriate level of working capital is determined by

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balancing the probability of insolvency against the profitability of current assets and liabilities

choices.label: B
choices.text: Evaluating the capital structure and dividend policy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Evaluating the capital leases used to finance fixed assets

choices.label: D
choices.text: Minimizing long-term debt because it is more expensive than short-term debt

questions.explanation: Holding more current assets and fewer current liabilities reduces the chance of being unable to pay, but idle liquid assets earn little, so profitability suffers. The right level is the point that balances those two, which is why working capital policy is a trade-off rather than a maximisation.
questions.explanationJa: 流動資産を厚く持ち流動負債を薄くすれば支払不能に陥る可能性は下がるが、遊休する流動資産はほとんど収益を生まないため収益性が犠牲になる。適切な水準はこの2つが釣り合う点であり、運転資本政策は最大化ではなくトレードオフの問題となる。

questions.stem: Which working capital policy has the greatest likelihood that a firm will be unable to meet obligations as they become due?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Financing all current assets with long-term debt

choices.label: B
choices.text: Financing all current assets with short-term debt

choices.label: C
choices.text: Financing fluctuating current assets with short-term debt and permanent current assets with equity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Financing fluctuating current assets with short-term debt and permanent current assets with long- term debt

questions.explanation: Funding every current asset with short-term debt means the whole balance must be refinanced repeatedly, including the permanent portion that never converts to cash. If credit tightens at a rollover date, the firm cannot pay. Matching permanent needs with long-term funds (D) avoids that exposure.
questions.explanationJa: すべての流動資産を短期債務で賄うと、現金化することのない恒常的な部分まで含めて、残高全体を繰り返し借り換えなければならない。借換時に信用が引き締まれば支払いができなくなる。恒常的な資金需要を長期資金で手当てする方法（D）ならこの危険を避けられる。

questions.stem: Which of the following ratios is most appropriate for evaluating the effectiveness of working capital management?
questions.explanation: Working capital management is about how efficiently the firm converts inventory and receivables into cash. Inventory turnover measures that directly for the largest and slowest-moving component. Debt-to-equity is a capital structure measure and return on assets is a profitability measure.
questions.explanationJa: 運転資本管理とは、在庫や売掛金をどれだけ効率よく現金化するかという問題である。棚卸資産回転率は、その中で最も金額が大きく回転の遅い要素について、これを直接測る。負債比率は資本構成、総資産利益率は収益性の指標であり、運転資本の運用効率を示さない。

questions.stem:
Yeats Company issued common stock for cash. What was the impact on the current ratio and net working capital?
Current ratio | Net working
capital
questions.explanation: Issuing stock for cash raises current assets while current liabilities are untouched. Net working capital therefore rises by the full amount. The current ratio also rises because adding the same amount to both parts of a ratio already above 1.0 would lower it, but here only the numerator grows.
questions.explanationJa: 現金と引き換えに株式を発行すると流動資産だけが増え、流動負債は変わらない。したがって正味運転資本はその全額だけ増加する。流動比率も上昇する。分子と分母に同額を足せば1.0超の比率は下がるが、ここでは分子だけが増えるためである。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the least likely reason for an entity to hold cash and marketable securities?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maintain sufficient cash to meet transaction requirements

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maintain a reserve for unexpected events

questions.explanation: Cash is held to settle transactions, to provide a buffer against surprises, and to satisfy compensating balance agreements. Maximising return is not a reason to hold cash; funds held for return would be invested in higher-yielding assets instead, and holding cash sacrifices yield for liquidity.
questions.explanationJa: 現金は、取引の決済のため、不測の事態への備えのため、そしてコンペンセイティング・バランスの要件を満たすために保有する。収益の最大化は現金を保有する理由にならない。収益を狙う資金であればより高利回りの資産に投じるはずで、現金の保有は利回りを犠牲にして流動性を得る選択である。

questions.stem: Brooks Company has daily cash receipts of $400,000. Brooks' bank offers a lockbox service that will reduce collection time by two days for $2,000 monthly fee. Brooks can earn 8% annually with any additional funds. What will be the annual increase to income before taxes from using the lockbox service?
questions.explanation: Two days of receipts are freed permanently: $400,000 x 2 = $800,000. Annual earnings on that = $800,000 x 8% = $64,000. Subtract the fee of $2,000 x 12 = $24,000, leaving a $40,000 increase in pretax income.
questions.explanationJa: 2日分の入金が恒常的に解放される: $400,000 × 2日 = $800,000。この資金の年間運用益 = $800,000 × 8% = $64,000。手数料 $2,000 × 12か月 = $24,000 を差し引き、税引前利益は $40,000 増加する。

questions.stem: An automated clearing house electronic funds transfer is

choices.label: A
choices.text: A check-like instrument drawn against the payor and rather than a bank

choices.label: C
choices.text: An electronic payment to a company's bank account

choices.label: D
choices.text: A transfer charge generated by an automated clearing house

questions.explanation: An ACH transfer moves funds electronically between bank accounts through a clearing network, with no paper instrument involved. It is the mechanism behind direct deposits and preauthorised payments.
questions.explanationJa: ACHによる資金移動は、清算ネットワークを通じて銀行口座間で電子的に資金を移すものであり、紙の証券は介在しない。給与の口座振込や事前承認による支払いはこの仕組みに基づいている。

questions.stem: Windfall Company has daily cash receipts of $300,000. Windfall's bank offers a lockbox service that will reduce collection time by four days for a $2,500 monthly fee. If money market rates average 3% for the year, what will be the annual impact on income before taxes from using the lockbox service?
questions.explanation: Funds released = $300,000 x 4 days = $1,200,000, earning $1,200,000 x 3% = $36,000 annually. The fee costs $2,500 x 12 = $30,000, so income before taxes rises by $6,000. The service is still worth using, but the margin is thin because the money market rate is low.
questions.explanationJa: 解放される資金 = $300,000 × 4日 = $1,200,000、その年間運用益 = $1,200,000 × 3% = $36,000。手数料は $2,500 × 12か月 = $30,000 なので、税引前利益は $6,000 増加する。導入する価値はあるが、短期金利が低いため margin は薄い。

questions.stem: Short-term unsecured notes issued by large corporations are called
questions.explanation: Commercial paper is unsecured short-term debt sold by large, financially strong corporations directly to investors. Agency securities come from government-sponsored enterprises, bankers' acceptances arise from trade transactions, and certificates of deposit are issued by banks.
questions.explanationJa: コマーシャルペーパーは、財務内容の良い大企業が投資家へ直接販売する無担保の短期債務である。エージェンシー証券は政府支援機関が発行し、銀行引受手形は貿易取引から生じ、譲渡性預金は銀行が発行する。

questions.stem: Commercial paper

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generally has interest rates lower than treasury bills

choices.label: B
choices.text: Has maturities of greater than 1 year

choices.label: D
choices.text: Typically does not have an active secondary market

questions.explanation: Commercial paper is usually bought to be held to maturity, so trading after issuance is thin. It also yields more than treasury bills because it carries credit risk, matures within 270 days to avoid registration, and is unsecured.
questions.explanationJa: コマーシャルペーパーは通常、満期保有目的で購入されるため、発行後の流通は薄い。また信用リスクを負う分、財務省短期証券より利回りは高く、登録義務を避けるため満期は270日以内で、無担保である。

questions.stem: Which of the following is least appropriate for use as a cash substitute?
questions.explanation: A cash substitute must return a known amount on a known date. Convertible bonds have long maturities and a value tied to the issuer's share price, so the amount recoverable on short notice is uncertain. Bankers' acceptances, commercial paper and treasury bills all mature within months at a fixed amount.
questions.explanationJa: 現金代替として使える資産は、確定した金額を確定した時期に回収できなければならない。転換社債は満期が長く、価値が発行会社の株価に連動するため、短期間で回収できる金額が不確実である。銀行引受手形・コマーシャルペーパー・財務省短期証券はいずれも数か月以内に確定額で満期を迎える。

questions.stem: Which of the following ratios is appropriate for the evaluation of accounts receivable?
questions.explanation: Days sales outstanding states how many days of sales remain uncollected, which measures directly how well receivables are being managed. Return on total assets and the current ratio look at the whole balance sheet rather than the receivable balance specifically.
questions.explanationJa: 売掛金回転日数（days sales outstanding）は、何日分の売上が未回収のまま残っているかを示し、売掛金の管理状況を直接測る。総資産利益率や流動比率は貸借対照表全体を見る指標であり、売掛金残高そのものを評価するものではない。

questions.stem: Stiffening Company is evaluating a proposed credit policy change. The proposed policy would change the average number of days for collection from 60 to 27 days and would reduce total sales by 25%, all of the decrease due to credit sales. Under the current policy, next year's sales are estimated at $128 million, with 75% of them being credit sales. Based on a 360-day year, what is the decrease in Stiffening's average accounts receivable balance of implementing the proposed credit policy change?
questions.explanation: Current credit sales = $128M x 75% = $96M, so receivables = $96M / 360 x 60 = $16M. After the change, total sales fall 25% to $96M and the entire $32M drop is in credit sales, leaving credit sales of $64M. New receivables = $64M / 360 x 27 = $4.8M. The decrease is $16M - $4.8M = $11.2M.
questions.explanationJa: 現行の信用売上 = $128M × 75% = $96M なので、売掛金 = $96M ÷ 360 × 60日 = $16M。変更後は総売上が25%減って $96M となり、減少分 $32M はすべて信用売上なので、信用売上は $64M。新しい売掛金 = $64M ÷ 360 × 27日 = $4.8M。減少額は $16M − $4.8M = $11.2M。

questions.stem: Evermore Company has average daily cash collections of $3 million, based on a 360-day year. A new system is estimated to reduce the average collection period by two days without affecting sales. The new system's annual cost is $100,000 plus 0.01% of collections. Evermore estimates that it would earn 6% on additional funds. What is the estimated annual net benefit from the new system?
questions.explanation: Funds released = $3M x 2 days = $6M, earning $6M x 6% = $360,000. The cost has two parts: the $100,000 fixed fee plus 0.01% of annual collections ($3M x 360 = $1,080M x 0.0001 = $108,000), totalling $208,000. Net benefit = $360,000 - $208,000 = $152,000. Missing the variable portion of the fee gives $260,000.

questions.stem: Pickle Pharmacy wants to determine the optimum safety stock level for drug Alpha. The annual carrying cost of Alpha is 25% of the inventory investment. The inventory investment averages $10 per unit. The stock out cost is estimated at $2 per unit. Pickle Pharmacy orders Alpha 20 times annually. Pickle Pharmacy defines the total costs of safety stock as carrying costs plus expected stock out costs. With 100 units of safety stock, there is a 15% probability of a 30-unit stock out per order cycle. What is the total annual cost of the 100 units of Alpha safety stock?
questions.explanation: Carrying cost of the safety stock = 100 units x $10 x 25% = $250. Expected stockout cost arises each order cycle: 15% x 30 units x $2 = $9 per cycle, and there are 20 cycles a year, so $180. Total = $250 + $180 = $430. Forgetting to multiply by the 20 order cycles gives $259.
questions.explanationJa: 安全在庫の保有コスト = 100単位 × $10 × 25% = $250。品切れコストは発注サイクルごとに発生し、1サイクルあたり 15% × 30単位 × $2 = $9、年間20サイクルなので $180。合計 = $250 + $180 = $430。年20回の発注サイクルを掛け忘れると $259 となる。

questions.stem: Which of the following inventory management approaches orders at the point where carrying costs equate nearest to restocking costs in order to minimize total inventory cost?
questions.explanation: The EOQ is derived by setting total ordering cost equal to total carrying cost, which is where their sum is minimised. Just-in-time seeks to eliminate inventory rather than optimise a batch size, MRP schedules materials from production plans, and ABC classifies items by value for control purposes.
questions.explanationJa: EOQは、発注コスト総額と保有コスト総額が等しくなる点として導かれ、そこで両者の合計が最小となる。ジャストインタイムはロットサイズの最適化ではなく在庫そのものの排除を目指し、MRPは生産計画から資材所要量を算定し、ABC分析は重要度に応じて品目を分類する管理手法である。

questions.stem: To determine the inventory reorder point, calculations normally include the
questions.explanation: The reorder point answers when to order, which depends on how fast stock is consumed and how long replenishment takes: average daily usage times lead time. Ordering cost, carrying cost and the EOQ all bear on how much to order, not when.
questions.explanationJa: 再発注点は「いつ発注するか」を決めるもので、在庫が消費される速さと補充に要する期間、すなわち1日平均使用量とリードタイムに依存する。発注コスト・保有コスト・EOQはいずれも「いくら発注するか」に関わる要素であって、発注時期には関係しない。

questions.stem: Stewpot Company uses the economic order model to determine the size of its purchase orders. What would cause an increase in the economic order quantity?
questions.explanation: EOQ is the square root of (2 x demand x ordering cost / carrying cost). A fall in carrying cost shrinks the denominator and therefore raises EOQ. Lower demand or lower ordering cost would shrink the numerator and reduce EOQ, and safety stock is outside the formula entirely.
questions.explanationJa: EOQは √(2 × 需要 × 発注コスト ÷ 保有コスト) である。保有コストの低下は分母を小さくするのでEOQは増加する。需要の減少や発注コストの低下は分子を小さくするためEOQは減少し、安全在庫はそもそもこの式に含まれない。

questions.stem: Baker manufacturers small appliances. Baker uses the economic order quantity model to determine the appropriate size of production runs or batches. What does Baker use as the order costs in the economic order quantity formula?
questions.explanation: For a manufacturer, the equivalent of placing an order is starting a production run, so the setup cost of reconfiguring the assembly line plays the role of ordering cost. Handling, insurance, taxes and storage all accrue while goods are held and are carrying costs.
questions.explanationJa: 製造業では、発注に相当するのは生産の開始であるため、組立ラインを再構成する段取コストが発注コストの役割を担う。荷役費・保険料・税金・保管費はいずれも在庫を保有している間に発生するので保有コストにあたる。

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to affect the optimal inventory level?
questions.explanation: The optimal level is determined by cost per unit, usage rate and order placement cost, all of which enter the EOQ calculation. How much happens to be on hand right now does not change what the optimal level is; it only tells you how far you are from it.
questions.explanationJa: 最適在庫水準は、単価・使用率・発注コストによって決まり、いずれもEOQの計算に入る要素である。現在たまたま手元にある在庫量は最適水準そのものを変えるものではなく、最適水準からどれだけ離れているかを示すにすぎない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to affect the inventory safety stock level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Degree of customer intolerance for backorders

choices.label: C
choices.text: Degree of shipment lead time uncertainty

questions.explanation: Safety stock exists to absorb uncertainty, so it depends on how variable demand and lead time are and how costly a stockout would be to the customer relationship. The cost of placing an order affects how large each order should be, not how much buffer is needed.
questions.explanationJa: 安全在庫は不確実性を吸収するために持つものなので、需要とリードタイムの変動の大きさ、そして品切れが顧客との関係に与える損失の大きさによって決まる。発注コストは1回の発注量に影響する要素であり、必要な緩衝在庫の量とは関係しない。

questions.stem: When would a retailer tend to increase the safety stock of inventory?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cost of running out of stock decreases

questions.explanation: More variable lead time means replenishment may arrive later than expected, so a larger buffer is needed to avoid running out. Higher carrying cost, a cheaper stockout, or steadier sales all point the other way and justify holding less safety stock.
questions.explanationJa: リードタイムの変動が大きくなると補充が想定より遅れる可能性が高まるため、品切れを避けるにはより厚い緩衝在庫が必要になる。保有コストの上昇、品切れコストの低下、売上の安定化はいずれも逆方向に働き、安全在庫を減らす根拠となる。

questions.stem: What is the largest source of short-term credit for small businesses?
questions.explanation: Small businesses buy on account from suppliers as a matter of course, and that trade credit arises without negotiation or credit standing tests. Commercial paper requires a high rating, debentures are long-term, and mortgages are secured long-term borrowing.
questions.explanationJa: 小規模事業者は日常的に仕入先から掛けで仕入れており、この企業間信用は交渉も信用力の審査もなく生じる。コマーシャルペーパーは高い格付を要し、社債は長期資金、抵当貸付は担保付の長期借入である。

questions.stem: Mason has a $400,000 loan with a stated 6% interest rate. Mason must maintain a 20% compensating balance in its checking account. Without the loan provisions, Mason otherwise would keep a zero balance in its checking account. What is the effective rate of interest on the loan?
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on the whole $400,000: $24,000. The 20% compensating balance leaves only $400,000 x 80% = $320,000 usable. Effective rate = $24,000 / $320,000 = 7.5%. The stated 6% understates the cost because the borrower pays interest on funds it cannot touch.
questions.explanationJa: 利息は借入額 $400,000 全額に課される: $24,000。20%のコンペンセイティング・バランスにより、実際に使えるのは $400,000 × 80% = $320,000。実効金利 = $24,000 ÷ $320,000 = 7.5%。表示金利6%が実態を過小に示すのは、使えない資金にも利息を払っているためである。

questions.stem: Capital projects may be classified by type of project. Which classification generally would be assigned to a project to retrofit equipment to meet new safety regulations?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expansion of existing products or markets

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expansion into new products or markets

questions.explanation: Retrofitting equipment to comply with new safety regulations is not undertaken to cut cost or grow revenue; it must be done to keep operating legally. Such projects are classified as mandated investments and are evaluated on how to comply at least cost rather than on return.
questions.explanationJa: 新しい安全規制に適合させるための設備改修は、原価削減や売上拡大のために行うものではなく、事業を合法的に継続するために不可欠な投資である。この種のプロジェクトは強制投資（mandated investments）に分類され、収益率ではなく最小の費用で要件を満たす方法として評価される。

questions.stem:
Yarrow Co. is considering the purchase of a new machine that costs $450,000. The new machine will generate net cash flow of $150,000 per year and net income of $100,000 per year for five years.
Yarrow's desired rate of return is 6%. The present value factor for a five-year annuity of $1, discounted at 6%, is 4.212. The present value factor of $1, at compound interest of 6% due in five years, is 0.7473.
What is the new machine's net present value?
questions.explanation: Net present value discounts cash flow, not net income: $150,000 x 4.212 = $631,800, less the $450,000 cost = $181,800. Using net income of $100,000 instead would give $421,200 - $450,000, a negative figure, which is why the income number is a distractor here.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値が割り引くのはキャッシュフローであり純利益ではない: $150,000 × 4.212 = $631,800、取得原価 $450,000 を差し引いて $181,800。純利益 $100,000 を使うと $421,200 − $450,000 とマイナスになる。設問の純利益はこの取り違えを誘う数値である。

questions.stem:
Vested, Inc. made some changes in operations and provided the following information:
Year 2 | Year 3
Operating revenues | $ 900,000 | $1,100,000
Operating expenses | 650,000 | 700,000
Operating assets | 1,200,000 | 2,000,000
What percentage represents the return on investment for year 3?
questions.explanation: Operating income for year 3 = $1,100,000 - $700,000 = $400,000. Investment is measured on AVERAGE operating assets = ($1,200,000 + $2,000,000) / 2 = $1,600,000. ROI = $400,000 / $1,600,000 = 25%. Using only the year-end assets would give 20% (choice D).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding the payback method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not consider the time value of money.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is the time required to recover the investment and earn a profit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a measure of how profitable one investment project is compared to another.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The salvage value of old equipment is ignored in the event of equipment replacement.

questions.explanation: Payback ignores discounting entirely, so it is blind to the time value of money. It measures recovery of the outlay, not profit (B); it says nothing about relative profitability (C); and salvage value of replaced equipment does reduce the net investment, so it is not ignored (D).
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間法は割引計算を一切行わないため、貨幣の時間価値を考慮できない。測るのは投資額の回収であって利益ではない（B）。プロジェクト間の相対的な収益性も示さない（C）。設備更新では旧設備の処分価額が正味投資額を減らすので無視されるわけでもない（D）。

questions.stem:
Minon, Inc. purchased a long-term asset on the last day of the current year. What are the effects of this purchase on return on investment and residual income?
Return on investment | Residual income
questions.explanation: Buying the asset on the last day adds to the investment base without giving the period any time to generate income from it. ROI's denominator grows while the numerator is unchanged, so ROI falls. Residual income falls too, because the capital charge rises with no offsetting income.
questions.explanationJa: 期末最終日に資産を取得すると、投資ベースだけが増え、その資産から当期の利益を生む時間はない。ROIは分母が増えて分子が変わらないため低下する。残余利益も、資本費用が増える一方でそれを打ち消す利益がないため減少する。

questions.stem:
Para Co. is reviewing the following data relating to an energy saving investment proposal:
Cost | $50,000
Residual value at the end of 5 years | 10,000
Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 5 years | 3.60
Present value of 1 due in 5 years at 12% | 0.57
What would be the annual savings needed to make the investment realize a 12% yield?
questions.explanation: To yield exactly 12%, net present value must be zero. The residual value contributes $10,000 x 0.57 = $5,700 of present value, so the annual savings must cover $50,000 - $5,700 = $44,300. Annual savings = $44,300 / 3.60 = $12,306. Ignoring the residual value would give $50,000 / 3.60 = $13,889, which is choice D.
questions.explanationJa: ちょうど12%の利回りを得るには正味現在価値がゼロになればよい。残存価額の現在価値は $10,000 × 0.57 = $5,700 なので、年間節約額で賄うべき金額は $50,000 − $5,700 = $44,300。年間節約額 = $44,300 ÷ 3.60 = $12,306。残存価額を無視すると $50,000 ÷ 3.60 = $13,889 となり、これが選択肢Dの誤答。

questions.stem: Lin Co. is buying machinery it expects will increase average annual operating income by $40,000. The initial increase in the required investment is $60,000, and the average increase in required investment is $30,000. To compute the accrual accounting rate of return, what amount should be used as the numerator in the ratio?
questions.explanation: The accrual accounting rate of return uses accounting income, not cash flow, in the numerator: the $40,000 increase in average annual operating income. The investment amounts belong in the denominator, where the average increase of $30,000 would be used if an average investment base is chosen.
questions.explanationJa: 会計的利益率の分子にはキャッシュフローではなく会計上の利益、すなわち平均年間営業利益の増加額 $40,000 を用いる。投資額は分母に入る要素であり、平均投資額を基準とする場合は平均増加額 $30,000 が分母となる。
