questions.stem: The profitability index is a variation on which of the following capital budgeting models?
questions.explanation: The profitability index divides the present value of future cash flows by the initial investment, using exactly the same discounted amounts as net present value. NPV states the result as a dollar amount while the index states it as a ratio, which makes it useful for ranking projects of different sizes.
questions.explanationJa: 収益性指数は将来キャッシュフローの現在価値を当初投資額で割ったもので、正味現在価値とまったく同じ割引後の金額を用いる。NPVが結果を金額で表すのに対し、指数は比率で表すため、規模の異なるプロジェクトの順位付けに使いやすい。

questions.stem:
Polo Co. requires higher rate of return for projects with a life span greater than five years. Projects extending beyond five years must earn a higher specified rate of return. Which of the following capital budgeting techniques can readily accommodate this requirement?
Internal rate of | Net present value
return
questions.explanation: Both techniques can handle a higher hurdle for longer projects. Net present value simply discounts those projects at the higher required rate, and internal rate of return computes each project's own return and compares it with the higher hurdle rate. Neither method is restricted to a single company-wide rate.
questions.explanationJa: どちらの手法も、期間の長いプロジェクトに高い要求水準を課すことに対応できる。正味現在価値法は、そのプロジェクトを高い要求収益率で割り引けばよい。内部収益率法は、各プロジェクト固有の収益率を計算し、高いハードルレートと比較すればよい。いずれも全社一律の率に縛られる手法ではない。

questions.stem: A proposed project has an expected economic life of eight years. In the calculation of the net present value of the proposed project, salvage value would be

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excluded from the calculation of the net present value

choices.label: B
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the future amount of the estimated salvage value

choices.label: C
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the estimated salvage value

choices.label: D
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the present value of the estimated salvage value

questions.explanation: Salvage value is a cash inflow received at the END of the project's life, so it must be discounted back to today before being compared with the initial outlay. Including it at its future amount (B) or at face value without discounting (C) would overstate net present value.
questions.explanationJa: 残存価額はプロジェクトの「終了時点」に受け取るキャッシュインフローなので、当初投資額と比較する前に現在価値へ割り引く必要がある。将来価値のまま含めたり（B）、割引せずに額面のまま含めたり（C）すると、正味現在価値を過大に評価してしまう。

questions.stem: A project should be accepted if the present value of cash flows from the project is
questions.explanation: Net present value is the present value of the cash flows less the initial investment, so NPV is positive exactly when that present value exceeds the outlay. Equal amounts (A) give NPV of zero, meaning the project earns precisely the required rate and is a matter of indifference.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値はキャッシュフローの現在価値から当初投資額を引いたものなので、現在価値が投資額を上回るときにNPVがプラスとなる。両者が等しい場合（A）はNPVがゼロ、すなわち要求収益率をちょうど達成する状態であり、採否は無差別となる。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Quest Co.'s Gold Division:
Sales | $311,000
Variable cost | 250,000
Traceable fixed costs | 50,000
Average invested capital | 40,000
Imputed interest rate | 10%
Quest's return on investment was
questions.explanation: Divisional operating income = $311,000 - $250,000 variable - $50,000 traceable fixed = $11,000. ROI = $11,000 / $40,000 average invested capital = 27.5%. The 10% imputed rate is used for residual income, not ROI.
questions.explanationJa: 部門営業利益 = $311,000 − 変動費 $250,000 − 個別固定費 $50,000 = $11,000。ROI = $11,000 ÷ 平均投下資本 $40,000 = 27.5%。帰属利子率10%は残余利益の計算で使うものであり、ROIには用いない。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Bala Co. for the year ended December 31, Year 1:
Sales | $600,000
Net income | 100,000
Capital investment | 400,000
Which of the following equations should be used to compute Bala's return on investment?
questions.explanation: ROI decomposes into asset turnover times return on sales: (sales / investment) x (net income / sales) = ($600 / $400) x ($100 / $600), which in the answer's shorthand is (6/4) x (1/6). The sales terms cancel, leaving net income over investment.
questions.explanationJa: ROIは資産回転率と売上高利益率の積に分解できる: (売上 ÷ 投資額) × (純利益 ÷ 売上) = ($600 ÷ $400) × ($100 ÷ $600)、これを選択肢の表記に直すと (6/4) × (1/6) となる。売上の項が約分され、純利益 ÷ 投資額が残る。

questions.stem: The invested capital-employed turnover rate would include
questions.explanation: A turnover rate measures how many dollars of sales each dollar of capital generates, so sales go on top and invested capital underneath. Placing net income in the numerator would give return on investment instead of a turnover measure.
questions.explanationJa: 回転率は、資本1ドルがどれだけの売上を生むかを測る指標なので、分子が売上、分母が投下資本となる。分子に純利益を置くと、回転率ではなく投下資本利益率になってしまう。

questions.stem:
Division A is considering a project that will earn a rate of return which is greater than the imputed interest charge for invested capital, but less than the division's historical return on invested capital. Division B is considering a project that will earn a rate of return which is greater than the division's historical return on invested capital, but less than the imputed interest charge for invested capital. If the objective is to maximize residual income, should these divisions accept or reject their projects?
Project A | Project B
questions.explanation: Residual income rises whenever a project earns more than the imputed interest charge, regardless of the division's historical ROI. Division A's project clears that hurdle and should be accepted even though it would dilute A's average return. Division B's project falls short of the charge and would reduce residual income, so it should be rejected.
questions.explanationJa: 残余利益は、プロジェクトの収益率が帰属利子率を上回れば、その部門の過去のROIがどうであれ増加する。A部門のプロジェクトはこの基準を満たすので、部門の平均収益率を下げるとしても採用すべきである。B部門のプロジェクトは帰属利子率に届かず残余利益を減らすため、却下すべきである。

questions.stem: Residual income of an investment center is the center's

choices.label: A
choices.text: Income plus the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: B
choices.text: Income less the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contribution margin plus the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contribution margin less the imputed interest on its invested capital

questions.explanation: Residual income starts from the center's income and subtracts a charge for the capital it uses: income - (invested capital x imputed rate). Subtracting the charge is what makes the measure show value created beyond the minimum required return. Contribution margin is before fixed costs and is not the starting point.
questions.explanationJa: 残余利益は、事業単位の利益から、使用した資本に対する賦課を差し引いて求める（利益 − 投下資本 × 帰属利子率）。この賦課を控除することで、最低限求められる収益を超えて生み出した価値が表れる。貢献利益は固定費控除前の数値であり、出発点にはならない。

questions.stem: What is the par value of common stock?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The value of the stock that must be entered as equity in the issuer’s financial statements

choices.label: B
choices.text: The value of the stock that must be entered as paid-in-capital in the issuer’s financial statements

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shareholder’s liability celling if the issuer goes bankrupt

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimated market value of the stock when it was issued

questions.explanation: Par value is a nominal legal amount that fixes the maximum a shareholder can be required to contribute. Once shares are paid up to par, the holder has no further liability to creditors if the issuer fails. It bears no relation to market value, and amounts received above par go to additional paid-in capital.
questions.explanationJa: 額面価額は法律上の名目金額であり、株主が拠出を求められうる上限を定めるものである。額面まで払込みが済んでいれば、発行会社が破綻しても株主が債権者に対してそれ以上の責任を負うことはない。市場価値とは無関係で、額面を超えて受け取った金額は資本剰余金に計上される。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not characteristic of venture capital?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lack of liquidity for some time period

questions.explanation: Venture capital typically begins with a private placement, takes common or convertible equity, and stays illiquid until an exit such as an IPO or sale. There is no fixed minimum holding period; the exit comes when the company is ready, which may be sooner or much later than five years.
questions.explanationJa: ベンチャーキャピタルは通常、私募から始まり、普通株や転換権付の持分を取得し、株式公開や売却といった出口までは流動性を欠いたままとなる。ただし最低保有期間が定まっているわけではない。出口は企業の状態次第であり、5年より早いことも、はるかに遅いこともある。

questions.stem: For the next 2 years, a lease is estimated to have an operating net cash inflow of $7,500 per annum, before adjusting for $5,000 per annum tax basis lease amortization, and a 40% tax rate. The present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 per year at 10% for 2 years is $1.74. What is the lease's after-tax present value using a 10% discount factor?
questions.explanation: Amortization is deductible but is not a cash outflow, so it only affects the tax. Taxable income = $7,500 - $5,000 = $2,500, tax = $2,500 x 40% = $1,000. After-tax cash flow = $7,500 - $1,000 = $6,500. Present value = $6,500 x 1.74 = $11,310. Taxing the full $7,500 would give $9,570 (choice C).
questions.explanationJa: リース償却費は損金にはなるがキャッシュの流出ではないため、税額にのみ影響する。課税所得 = $7,500 − $5,000 = $2,500、税額 = $2,500 × 40% = $1,000。税引後キャッシュフロー = $7,500 − $1,000 = $6,500。現在価値 = $6,500 × 1.74 = $11,310。$7,500 全額に課税すると $9,570（選択肢C）となる。

questions.stem:
Which of the following would a rational investor consider when purchasing an entity for cash?
I. The cash paid to the entity's current shareholders
II. The after-tax cash flow from operations III. The present value of the entity's liabilities
questions.explanation: A cash purchase of the entity means acquiring its obligations along with its operations, so all three matter: the price paid to current shareholders, the after-tax cash the business will generate, and the present value of the liabilities that come with it. Ignoring the liabilities would overstate what the buyer is really getting.
questions.explanationJa: 現金による企業買収は、事業とともにその債務も引き受けることを意味するため、3つすべてが判断材料となる。現株主に支払う対価、事業が生み出す税引後キャッシュ、そして引き継ぐ負債の現在価値である。負債を無視すると、買手が実際に得るものを過大に評価してしまう。

questions.stem: Fluid Company's current assets increased by $120 and current liabilities decreased by $200. Fluid's net working capital
questions.explanation: Net working capital = current assets - current liabilities. Assets rose $120 and liabilities fell $200, so the change is $120 - (-$200) = an increase of $320. Subtracting rather than adding the liability decrease gives the $80 decrease in choice B.
questions.explanationJa: 正味運転資本 = 流動資産 − 流動負債。流動資産が $120 増え、流動負債が $200 減ったので、変化は $120 − (−$200) = $320 の増加となる。負債の減少を加算せずに減算すると、選択肢Bの $80 減少という誤りになる。

questions.stem: Advantage Company writes and receives checks totaling $1,000 daily. It takes five days for Advantage's checks to clear its account, but only three days for Advantage's deposits to be available for use. What is the amount of Advantage's float?
questions.explanation: Disbursement float = $1,000 x 5 days = $5,000, the money still in the account after checks are written. Collection float = $1,000 x 3 days = $3,000, deposits not yet usable. Net float = $5,000 - $3,000 = $2,000 in the company's favour.
questions.explanationJa: 支払フロート = $1,000 × 5日 = $5,000。小切手を振り出した後もまだ口座に残っている資金である。回収フロート = $1,000 × 3日 = $3,000。入金したがまだ使えない資金である。純フロート = $5,000 − $3,000 = $2,000 で、企業にとって有利な方向となる。

questions.stem: When would a business most likely offer credit terms of 2/10, net 30?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The business can borrow funds only at a rate higher than the effective annual interest rate of these terms.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The business can borrow funds at a rate lower than the effective annual interest rate of these terms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Competitors are offering the same terms and the business has a cash shortage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Competitors are not offering terms and the business has a cash surplus.

questions.explanation: Terms of 2/10, net 30 cost the seller roughly 36% on an annual basis, so they are only worth offering when something else compels it: competitors already offer the same terms, and the seller needs cash sooner. A firm that can borrow more cheaply (B) would borrow instead of granting such an expensive discount.
questions.explanationJa: 2/10, net 30 という条件は、売手にとって年率換算でおよそ36%のコストとなるため、他に事情がある場合にのみ提示する価値がある。すなわち、競合が既に同条件を出しており、かつ自社が早期に現金を必要としている場合である。より低い金利で借りられる企業（B）なら、これほど高コストの割引を与えるより借入を選ぶ。

questions.stem: Raking Company is basing next year's budget on sales of $36 million. Raking offers credit terms of 1/10, n/30 and expects that 80% of sales will be on credit, with discounts taken on 50% of the credit sales. What are estimated discounts taken by customers for next year?
questions.explanation: Work through the layers: credit sales = $36M x 80% = $28.8M; discounts are taken on half of that = $14.4M; the discount is 1% = $144,000. Applying the 1% to all credit sales would give $288,000, and to total sales $360,000.
questions.explanationJa: 段階を追って計算する。信用売上 = $36M × 80% = $28.8M。そのうち半分で割引が利用されるので $14.4M。割引率は1%なので $144,000。信用売上全額に1%を適用すると $288,000、総売上に適用すると $360,000 となり、いずれも誤り。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
What is the net present value?
questions.explanation: The savings are a level annual amount, so use the annuity factor: $20,000 x 5.65 = $113,000. Net present value = $113,000 - $100,000 = $13,000. There is no residual value, so the single-sum factor 0.322 is not needed.
questions.explanationJa: 節約額は毎年一定なので年金現価係数を使う: $20,000 × 5.65 = $113,000。正味現在価値 = $113,000 − $100,000 = $13,000。残存価額がないため、一時金の現価係数 0.322 は使わない。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
What is the accrual accounting rate of return based on initial investment?
questions.explanation: The accrual rate of return uses accounting income, so depreciation must be subtracted from the cash savings: $100,000 / 10 years = $10,000 depreciation, giving income of $20,000 - $10,000 = $10,000. Based on the INITIAL investment, the rate = $10,000 / $100,000 = 10%. Using the cash savings without deducting depreciation would give 20% (choice B).
questions.explanationJa: 会計的利益率は会計上の利益を用いるため、キャッシュ節約額から減価償却費を控除する: $100,000 ÷ 10年 = $10,000 の減価償却費、利益 = $20,000 − $10,000 = $10,000。「当初」投資額基準なので、利益率 = $10,000 ÷ $100,000 = 10%。減価償却を引かずにキャッシュ節約額のまま計算すると20%（選択肢B）となり誤る。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
In estimating the internal rate of return, the factors in the table of present values of an annuity should be taken from columns closest to what amount?
questions.explanation: The internal rate of return is the discount rate that makes net present value zero, so $100,000 = $20,000 x factor, giving factor = $100,000 / $20,000 = 5.00. You then scan the 10-period row of the annuity table for the rate whose factor is closest to 5.00. The 5.65 factor corresponds to the 12% hurdle rate, not to the IRR.
questions.explanationJa: 内部収益率は正味現在価値をゼロにする割引率なので、$100,000 = $20,000 × 係数 から 係数 = $100,000 ÷ $20,000 = 5.00。年金現価表の10期の行で、係数が 5.00 に最も近い率を探すことになる。係数 5.65 は要求収益率12%に対応する値であり、IRRの手がかりではない。

questions.stem: A multiperiod project has a positive net present value. Which of the following statements is correct regarding its required rate of return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less than the company’s weighted average cost of capital

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less than the project’s internal rate of return

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greater than the company’s weighted average cost of capital

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greater than the project’s internal rate of return

questions.explanation: A positive net present value means the cash flows are worth more than the outlay when discounted at the required rate, which happens only when the project earns more than that rate. Since the internal rate of return IS the project's earned rate, the required rate must be below it.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値がプラスであるとは、要求収益率で割り引いてもキャッシュフローの価値が投資額を上回るということであり、これはプロジェクトが要求収益率を超えて稼いでいる場合にのみ起こる。内部収益率はまさにそのプロジェクトが稼ぐ率なので、要求収益率はそれより低いことになる。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
What is the net present value of the project?
questions.explanation: Helm is tax-exempt, so the cash savings need no tax adjustment: $130,000 x 3.60 (the 12% annuity factor) = $468,000. Net present value = $468,000 - $400,000 = $68,000. Depreciation is not a cash flow and does not enter the NPV calculation.
questions.explanationJa: Helmは免税団体なのでキャッシュ節約額に税調整は不要: $130,000 × 3.60（12%の年金現価係数）= $468,000。正味現在価値 = $468,000 − $400,000 = $68,000。減価償却費はキャッシュフローではないため、NPVの計算には入れない。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
What is the internal rate of return on this project?
questions.explanation: At the IRR, $400,000 = $130,000 x factor, so the required factor = 3.077. Annuity factors fall as the rate rises, and even the 16% factor is 3.30, still above 3.077. The rate that produces 3.077 must therefore be higher than 16%.
questions.explanationJa: IRRでは $400,000 = $130,000 × 係数 が成り立つので、必要な係数 = 3.077。年金現価係数は割引率が上がるほど小さくなるが、16%の係数でも 3.30 とまだ 3.077 を上回っている。したがって係数 3.077 をもたらす率は16%より高い。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
For the project's first year, what would be Helm's accounting rate of return, based on the project's average book value for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Accounting income = cash savings $130,000 - depreciation ($400,000 / 5 = $80,000) = $50,000. Average book value in year 1 = (beginning $400,000 + ending $320,000) / 2 = $360,000. Rate = $50,000 / $360,000 = 13.9%. Using the initial $400,000 instead would give 12.5% (choice A).

questions.stem:
Able Company has two mutually exclusive projects, A and B, which have the same initial investment requirements and lives. Project B has a decrease in estimated cash inflows each year, and project A has an increase in estimated net cash inflows each year. Project A has a greater total net cash inflow.
Diagram I below depicts the original estimate of net cash inflows of each project by year. Diagram II depicts the original estimate of net present value (NPV) of each project assuming various discount rates.
Which of the two projects would have the greater payback period and average accounting rate of return (ARR)?
Payback period | Average ARR
questions.explanation: Project A's inflows start small and rise, so it takes longer to recover the outlay: A has the longer payback period. The average accounting rate of return is driven by total income over the life, and A has the greater total net cash inflow with the same investment, so A also has the higher average ARR. Neither measure discounts, so the timing advantage of B does not help it here.
questions.explanationJa: プロジェクトAはキャッシュ流入が小さく始まって年々増えるため、投資額の回収に時間がかかる。したがって回収期間はAの方が長い。平均会計的利益率は全期間の利益総額で決まり、投資額が同じでAの方が総流入額が大きいので、平均ARRもAの方が高い。どちらの指標も割引を行わないため、Bの「早く回収できる」という利点はここでは効かない。

questions.stem:
Able Company has two mutually exclusive projects, A and B, which have the same initial investment requirements and lives. Project B has a decrease in estimated cash inflows each year, and project A has an increase in estimated net cash inflows each year. Project A has a greater total net cash inflow.
Diagram I below depicts the original estimate of net cash inflows of each project by year. Diagram II depicts the original estimate of net present value (NPV) of each project assuming various discount rates.
Due to innovation, both projects will terminate at the end of Year 4 with cash flows remaining as projected for the first 4 years and no cash flows in Year 5. Which of the two projects would have the greater internal rate of return under the original estimate and the estimate made in light of the new circumstances?
Original estimates | New estimates
questions.explanation: Under the original estimates B earns the higher internal rate of return because its inflows arrive early, and IRR rewards early cash regardless of the total. Cutting off Year 5 removes A's largest inflow while barely touching B, whose cash had already been received, so B remains higher under the new estimates as well.
questions.explanationJa: 当初の見積りではBの内部収益率が高い。Bは流入が早い時期に集中しており、IRRは総額にかかわらず早期のキャッシュを高く評価するためである。5年目を打ち切ると、後年に流入が偏るAは最大の流入を失う一方、Bは既に回収済みでほとんど影響を受けない。したがって新しい見積りでもBの方が高いままとなる。

questions.stem:
Harvey Co. is evaluating a capital investment proposal for a new machine. The investment proposal shows the following information.
Initial cost | $500,000
Life | 10 years
Annual net cash inflows | $200,000
Salvage value | $100,000
If acquired, the machine will be depreciated using the straight-line method. The payback period for this investment is
questions.explanation: Payback divides the initial cost by the annual net cash inflow: $500,000 / $200,000 = 2.5 years. Salvage value is received at the end of the tenth year and therefore cannot shorten the time needed to recover the outlay, and depreciation is not a cash flow.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間は当初投資額を年間正味キャッシュ流入額で割って求める: $500,000 ÷ $200,000 = 2.5年。残存価額は10年目の末に受け取るものなので投資額の回収期間を短縮できない。また減価償却費はキャッシュフローではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strength of the payback method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It considers cash flows for all years of the project.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It distinguishes the sources of cash inflows.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It considers the time value of money.

questions.explanation: The payback method's appeal is its simplicity: it needs no discount rate and produces a figure that is easy to communicate. Its weaknesses are the mirror image of the other choices, since it ignores cash flows after the payback point, does not distinguish their sources, and applies no discounting.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間法の利点はその簡便さにある。割引率を必要とせず、結果も伝えやすい。他の選択肢は、いずれも回収期間法の弱点をそのまま裏返した記述である。回収時点より後のキャッシュフローを無視し、その源泉を区別せず、割引計算も行わない。
